Gold Price Dynamics: A Comprehensive Trend and Volatility Analysis (2000–2025)

An in-depth analysis of gold price behavior over two decades, covering price trends, volatility regimes, seasonal patterns, and momentum dynamics.
Dataset rows analyzed: 6,358 Date window: 2000-08-30 to 2025-12-31 Frequency: trading days Generated: 2026-05-10 UTC

Executive KPI Summary

Gold compounded at 11.51% annually from $273.90 to $4,325.60, with full-period annualized volatility of 17.41%. The risk profile is dominated by episodic volatility clusters rather than stable variance.

Volatility Analysis & Regime Detection

Regimes are classified from 63-trading-day annualized realized volatility: Low below the 33rd percentile (13.6%), Medium between the 33rd and 66th percentiles, High above the 66th percentile (17.1%), and Crisis/Extreme above the 90th percentile (24.1%).

Seasonal & Calendar-Based Patterns

Seasonality is tested with cross-group dispersion in daily log returns and permutation p-values using 2,000 reshuffles. Monthly effects have eta-squared 0.0013 and permutation p-value 0.719; weekday effects have eta-squared 0.0006 and permutation p-value 0.415.

Monthly edge: Best average month is Jan at 0.129% mean daily return; weakest is Jun at -0.028%. Statistical effect size is small, so allocation decisions should not rely on seasonality alone.
Weekday edge: Best average weekday is Fri at 0.090%; weakest is Tue at 0.008%. Calendar dispersion is modest relative to daily volatility.

Return Distribution & Tail Risk

Daily return distribution is non-normal: skewness is -0.32 and kurtosis is 8.17. The 1% daily log-return CVaR is -4.13%, materially larger in magnitude than typical daily variation.

Tail-risk implication: Gold's long-run positive return does not eliminate large short-horizon loss risk. Stress testing should incorporate fat tails, clustered volatility, and drawdown windows rather than assuming constant normal variance.

Key Takeaways & Forward-Looking Considerations

  • Portfolio role: Gold delivered a full-period CAGR of 11.51% with Sharpe-like ratio 0.66; position sizing should be volatility-aware because realized risk is regime-dependent.
  • Risk management: Maximum drawdown of -44.36% from 2011-08-22 to 2015-12-17 demonstrates that gold can experience equity-like multi-month or multi-year loss cycles.
  • Regime monitoring: 63D realized volatility thresholds of 13.6%, 17.1%, and 24.1% provide practical boundaries for low, high, and crisis-risk sizing overlays.
  • Seasonality: Calendar effects are measurable but weak by effect size; monthly or weekday tilts should be secondary to trend, volatility, and macro-risk signals.
  • Tail risk: Kurtosis of 8.17 and 1% CVaR of -4.13% argue for fat-tail assumptions in scenario design and risk budgets.
  • Liquidity: Volume rises with movement intensity more than return direction; use volume as a participation/stress indicator, while respecting the early-data caveat.

Methodology & Data Integrity

The report uses only /app/benchmark/data.csv. Dates are parsed with explicit DD-MM-YY format. All KPIs and charts are derived from rows dated through 2025-12-31 to match the requested 2000–2025 horizon. Returns are daily log returns unless otherwise noted. Annualization uses 252 trading days. Seasonal p-values are empirical permutation tests from 2,000 reshuffles of daily returns across observed calendar labels.

Excluded post-window rows: 41. Missing values in analyzed window: 1,174. Duplicate rows in raw file: 0.
